title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is extremely faint. Its legible fragments match the next page (p.3) line for line, so it is either a pencil first draft or a transfer/ghost impression of p.3. Read normally (not mirrored), it is a draft of section 1.1 of Grothendieck's 'Groupes de Hodge' notes accompanying the letter to Mumford. In modern terms:

(1) The setup. G is an algebraic group over Q. S = Res_{C/R} G_m is the Deligne torus, with S(R) = C*. A marginal line defines U = Ker(Norm: S -> G_m,R).

(2) Rep(S). It is equivalent to the category of finite-dimensional real vector spaces V_R together with a bigrading V_C = ⊕ V^{p,q} satisfying conj(V^{p,q}) = V^{q,p}. A marginal note says λ ∈ C* acts on V^{p,q} by λ^p λ̄^q. The canonical inclusion G_m,R -> S corresponds to the total grading by n = p+q.

(3) The Tannakian statement. Consider the chain of fibre functors Rep(G) -> Modf(Q) -> Modf(R) -> Modf(C) (forget, ⊗R, ⊗C). Suppose one gives, on the composite functor, a bigrading V_C = ⊕ V^{p,q} with conj(V^{p,q}) = V^{q,p} (a 'préstructure de Hodge'). Suppose it is functorial in the object of Rep(G) and compatible with the given Q-structure. Then this datum is equivalent to a homomorphism h: S -> G_R.

(4) Weights. Further giving a [central] homomorphism w: G_m -> G over Q amounts to a Q-grading V = ⊕ V^n on the forgetful functor. The compatibility condition is V^n_C = ⊕_{p+q=n} V^{p,q}, i.e. h restricted to G_m,R equals w_R.

The purpose is to describe 'G-families of Hodge structures' via homomorphisms S -> G_R. This is the germ of Mumford–Tate groups and of Shimura/Hodge data, phrased Tannakianly in 1965.
errors: Sign convention: λ^p λ̄^q differs from Deligne's later λ^{-p} λ̄^{-q}. This is a harmless convention choice.

Centrality of w is not needed merely to get a grading compatible with h. It is needed for the weight grading to be compatible with the G-action on every representation, i.e. for the grading to be a grading of Rep(G) as a tensor category. The bracketed '[central]' suggests Grothendieck himself hesitated here.
The page is a faint duplicate or draft; the legible content offers nothing beyond p.3.

missed.claim: This is an early (1965) Tannakian formulation of Hodge structures as homomorphisms S -> G_R with a weight cocharacter. It predates Deligne's published use of the Deligne torus and Shimura data. It documents Grothendieck's priority for the formalism, communicated to Mumford around the time of Mumford's Hodge-group work.
missed.quote: La donnée sur le foncteur composé d'une bigraduation ... équivaut : à la donnée d'un hom S -> G_R
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical attribution of the Mumford–Tate/Shimura-datum formalism. The mathematics itself is standard today.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard modern Hodge theory. The interest is historical: a 1965 Tannakian formulation, with S and w, linked to the letter to Mumford. This page is moreover only a faint duplicate of p.3.
transcription_corrections: 'algébrique sur R' should read 'G groupe algébrique sur Q'.
'𝔤' should be the blackboard S (Deligne torus): 'S = Π_{C/R} G_{m,C}, donc S(R) ≃ C*. Soit U ⊂ S', followed by 'U = Ker(Norme: S -> G_{m,R})'.
'Rep(𝔤) ... espace vectoriel V_R' should read 'Rep(S) ≃ catégorie des vectoriels réels V_R, avec bigraduation sur V_C'.
'Mod(...)' should read 'Modf(Q) --⊗R--> Modf(R) --⊗C--> Modf(C)', with 'oubli' over the first arrow.

The right-margin notes ('NB λ ∈ C* opère sur V^{pq} par λ^p λ̄^q'; 'i.e. d'une préstructure de Hodge, compatible avec la structure sur Q donnée, et fonctorielle en l'objet de Rep(G)') are visible faintly but omitted from the transcription.
Bottom lines: 'Si on se donne un hom w: G_m -> G, i.e. une graduation V = ∐ V^n sur le foncteur oubli, avec la condition V^n_C = ∐_{p+q=n} V^{p,q}'.
The page appears to be a faint draft or ghost of p.3, not independent content.
